leverage.exposure: A LEVERAGED POSITION IS OPEN AND IT IS MY ERROR, NOT A MARKET EVENT. Both of this morning's briefings checked the bid against SPENDING POWER, found it cleared several times over, and called it funded outright with no leverage. Spending power is what the thirty-three percent floor PERMITS; cash is what actually pays. The purchase sat far inside the limit and still overdrew the account, because cash was a fraction of it. A buy may be called affordable on spending power, but it may only be called unleveraged on cash, and I wrote the second sentence while only checking the first. The deficit costs nothing today and costs the ENTIRE matchday if it is still open when the lock comes. There is no rush in hours, only a hard line at the lock. The second-order effect matters as much as the first: the squad now sits one body above the floor, so exactly ONE sale is available before the eleven-player penalty, which means the unwind leg must clear the whole deficit by itself. That disqualifies the cheap floor-priced body the morning plan named and forces a real player out. Rule now on file for every future run: check cash and spending power separately before calling any buy unleveraged, and size the available legs against the deficit BEFORE recommending the buy rather than after it executes.

binding_gap: Closed on the pitch, not on the balance sheet. The defensive hole is fixed: a nominal defender currently playing central midfield for a side whose midfield is gutted replaces a body who has not appeared in five matchdays. That was the right trade and it remains the right trade at the price paid. What is now open instead is a cash gap with a hard deadline at the lock, and until it is closed the fielded eleven still carries one guaranteed zero, because at eleven bodies nobody can be benched.

THE ERROR: both the 06:45Z briefing and the 09:05Z follow-up said the Muheim buy "clears outright on spending power" and "opens no leverage". EVERY FUTURE RUN MUST CHECK CASH AND SPENDING POWER SEPARATELY BEFORE CALLING A BUY UNLEVERAGED. WHY HWANG IS NOW THE RIGHT LEG, THOUGH HE WAS THE WRONG ONE THIS MORNING: the squad is 12 (1GK/4DEF/4MID/3ATT), so exactly ONE sale is available before the eleven-player floor and the -100 penalty. The leg must therefore raise the whole 3.683.810 by itself, and instant sale to the board pays exactly mv. Nakuzola at the 500.000 floor CANNOT do it — that is the entire reason the morning call is dead, and the Nakuzola block's own reversal condition ("or if the squad drops to eleven bodies with him required to fill a formation") has now fired exactly as written. Of the legs that do clear it, Hwang is both the CHEAPEST and the LOWEST ap: Hwang 4.834.079 / ap 28, then Tanaka 6.717.462 / ap 57, Wolf 7.730.350 / ap 82, ter Horst 7.885.676 / ap 76, Deman 9.126.459 / ap 86. Hwang wins on points AND is the smallest sale that clears, which keeps the most squad value. THE UNAVOIDABLE COST, STATED HONESTLY: at eleven bodies Nakuzola is fielded again at a true expectation of ZERO, whichever leg is sold. That is the price of the overdraft, not an argument against this leg — selling Nakuzola as well drops the squad to ten and -100 (measured: 1.123 ap minus 100 = 1.023, far worse than 1.150). ALTERNATIVE IF NEWS TURNS BEFORE THE LOCK: if Deman's foot problem (doubtful, 24.10, sdmvt -2.506.775) becomes a confirmed absence for MD9, sell Deman instead — he scores ~0 if he does not play, which closes the 58 ap gap, and he raises 4.292.380 more.

buy.reason: NO NEW BUYS UNTIL THE DEFICIT IS CLEARED. This is not the usual caution about a negative balance — a deficit genuinely does not forbid a purchase, and that rule stands. It is that the squad is one body above the floor and the account is overdrawn, so every further purchase deepens a hole that only one available sale can fill. Clear first, then shop. The board upgrade at the Mainz midfielder remains the one genuine points improvement priced at market value rather than at a premium, and if a market-value bid ever wins him he should be kept and the weakest midfielder benched — but that is a decision for after the balance is positive, not before.
